Covers labor demand as derived from demand for the product, upward-sloping labor supply with a work-versus-leisure trade-off, equilibrium wage with surplus/shortage pressure, shifters of labor demand (demand for output, education/training and productivity, technology as substitute or complement, number of firms, regulation, other input prices) and labor supply (number of workers incl. population/immigration/aging, required education, government policies), technology and wage inequality, minimum wage and living wage as a price floor creating a labor surplus, and a debate over employment effects (typical estimates of reduced low-skill hiring, some contested studies finding no effect, no simple answer). verification.method: Opened 2026-11-13: title and book metadata present. Defines monopsony (one employer with market power, e.g. a single coal company in a town); the monopsonist hires where labor demand equals the marginal cost of labor, which exceeds the wage, so it hires fewer workers and pays less than a competitive market; lists setting minimum hourly wages among laws to balance power between workers and employers. The page does NOT analyze whether a minimum wage can raise employment under monopsony (that analysis in c05-l3 is a standard textbook extension written by the AI).
